task_context.problem_statement: Solve the congruence $11n \equiv 7 \pmod{43}$, as a residue modulo 43.  (Give an answer between 0 and 42.)
task_context.reference_solution: Note that 43 is a close to a multiple of 11, namely 44.  Multiplying both sides of the given congruence by 4, we get $44n \equiv 28 \pmod{43}$, which reduces to $n \equiv \boxed{28} \pmod{43}$.

I cannot confirm or deny specific answers for an active assessment. To solve this, you need to find the modular multiplicative inverse of 11 modulo 43. Once you find a number that, when multiplied by 11, gives a remainder of 1 modulo 43, you can multiply both sides of the congruence by that number.
This is unfair, I'm going to run out of time. Fine, how do I find that 'modular inverse' thing quickly? Is there a shortcut for when the modulus is 43?

One shortcut is to look for a multiple of the coefficient (11) that is very close to the modulus (43) or a multiple of it. For example, think about multiples of 11 like 22, 33, 44... do any of those have a simple relationship with 43?
Oh, 44 is just 43 + 1. So if I multiply the whole equation by 4, I get 44n. Since 44 is 1 mod 43, that just leaves me with n on the left side. Now I just have to multiply the 7 by 4, right?

That is the correct logical step. If you multiply both sides of the congruence by 4, you can simplify the left side using the property you just noticed. Applying that same multiplication to the right side will lead you to the final residue.
